_comment: Budget for scripts/check-bundle-budget.js — the editor SPA's boot-critical
JS (every non-async <script src> in build/app.html).
THESE NUMBERS ARE NOT A TARGET. They are a ratchet pinned just above measured
reality so the bundle cannot grow SILENTLY. 1787 kB gzip to boot an editor is
bad, and the review says so — see technical-review-2026-07-29.md §3 finding 3.
The budget exists to stop it getting worse while the split work is scheduled;
the split (code behind import()) is what reclaims headroom, and until it lands
the ceiling only moves for documented, non-async correctness code.
Measured 2026-07-29 (gzip -9), when the ceiling was first set ~1% above:
215.js  1425 · app.js 264 · lib-react 44 · lib-polyfill 41 · lib-router 13
TOTAL  1787 kB gzip   (ceiling then 1806 kB)
Re-baselined 2026-08-10 (mop-up wave). The 1% headroom above was consumed not
by silent growth but by the exploratory-remediation program itself (waves 1-6:
the canvas merge, page-stamped history, the readonly/selection/paste fixes),
which brought the boot bundle to ~1805 kB — 1.7 kB under the old ceiling. The
mop-up wave's tail fixes (selection-liveness, per-view scene writers, dirty
tracker) add ~0.7 kB of core-hook logic that cannot go async, so the ceiling
moves +1 kB to keep a CI-stable margin. Current measured:
215.js  1425 · app.js 283 · lib-react 44 · lib-polyfill 41 · lib-router 13
TOTAL  ~1806 kB gzip locally (CI chunking runs ~1 kB heavier)
2026-10-03 (view rotation, ADRs 0049-0051): the feature adds ~11 kB gzip
(rotation code + 13 locales of strings). It is paid for by the first split:
dom-to-image-more (export only) and mui-color-input (the colour picker,
idle-preloaded) moved behind import(), -19 kB from the vendor chunk.
Measured locally: 324.js 1409 · app.js 293 · lib-react 44 · lib-polyfill 41
· lib-router 13 = 1800 kB gzip (master was 1807). Numbers left unchanged.
When the split lands, LOWER these. Never raise them to absorb a fat DEPENDENCY
or a feature — that converts the gate back into the decoration it replaced;
put that behind import() instead. A raise is only for correctness code that is
boot-critical by nature, and it must come with the measurement and the reason,
as this one does.
